ACT-J01
By focusing on stairs—an obstacle for her and
many others—Long hopes to raise awareness
about accessibility in the music world.
As of 2023, Long’s project includes over
190 portraits. One features the artist Laurel, who
perches on a lone step attached to a stage. In another,
singer Amy Shark crouches at the bottom of an
auditorium staircase. Despite showcasing artists,
Long wants to send a message.
PASSAGE II
To Slide the Great Wall
] My grandma and I look out past towering pines
and cedars to admire the lengthy path the Great Wall of
China carves into the distant mountains. [
] She would
rather I be fully absorbed, like her, in the history of this
The writer is considering deleting the underlined por-
tion (adjusting the punctuation as needed). Should the
underlined portion be kept or deleted?
A.
Kept, because it helps clarify how the theme of
stairs is related to Long’s goal of raising aware-
ness about accessibility.
B.
Kept, because it offers insight into the various
types of obstacles that Long intends to focus on in
her photo series.
C.
Deleted, because it is unrelated to the paragraph’s
explanation of why stairs are an accessibility issue
for wheelchair users.
D.
Deleted, because it is unrelated to the paragraph’s
discussion of Long’s portrait of the singer Mallrat.
Which choice most clearly indicates that Long’s aim is
to both showcase artists and send a message?
F.
No Change
G.
In addition to
H.
Rather than
J.
Before
Given that all the following sentences include actual
quotations from Long, which one, if added here, would
most effectively conclude the paragraph and essay?
A.
“If I want to go to an arena show,” she explains, “I
don’t even bother booking wheelchair-accessible
seats anymore.”
B.
“Being at a concert with a camera in my hands is
my ultimate happy place,” she says.
C.
“Everyone,” she emphasizes, “deserves to be able
to access and enjoy live music.”
D.
“I started photographing as many artists as I could
get ahold of,” she says.
The writer is considering revising the underlined por-
tion to the following:
serpentine
Given that the information is accurate, should the
writer make this revision?
F.
Yes, because the revision more vividly describes
the appearance of the wall in the distance.
G.
Yes, because the revision helps specify how long
the wall is.
H.
No, because the revision provides a descriptive
detail that is out of place in an informative essay.
J.
No, because the revision fails to establish why the
wall was built.
